description: Evidence captured at a customer's door: a photo, a signature or an OTP, with the coordinates the courier stood at.

fields.description: The courier who captured this proof, resolved server-side from the session — never sent by the client.
fields.label: Courier

fields.description: Photo or signature image. Empty for an OTP proof, and empty while a queued offline upload has not landed yet.
fields.label: File

fields.description: When the courier captured this on the handset — NOT when the server received it. The two differ by hours for a proof that was queued offline.
fields.label: Captured At

fields.description: Client-generated idempotency key. A retried upload from the offline queue reuses it, so the same tap can never produce two proofs.
fields.label: Request ID

fields.description: GPS accuracy radius in metres, as reported by the handset.
fields.label: Accuracy (m)

fields.description: Set when the handset reported a mock location provider. Such a proof is stored but must never be promoted into the address pin consensus.
fields.label: Is Mocked

fields.description: Which build captured this proof. Blank and "android" both mean a native capture, which reports Position.isMocked and therefore carries mock-GPS evidence. "web" means the browser build, where geolocator_web exposes no isMocked and iOS has no mock-provider signal at all — such a proof is unverifiable by construction and consensus promotes it at courier_web (35) rather than courier_verified (40). Blank is deliberately treated as android so every pre-existing proof keeps the behaviour it was written under.
fields.label: Capture Platform

name: Delivery Proof
